$comment: GENERATED by engine/src/ledger_engine/protocol/schema.py from the engine's message models (ADR-0054). Do not edit: run `engine/.venv/bin/python -I -m ledger_engine.protocol.schema > contracts/engine-protocol.schema.json`.
title: Finzytrack engine protocol
description: The plain-data protocol between the main sidecar and the ledger engine. JSON Lines: one request per line on the engine's stdin, one reply per line on its protocol channel (its original stdout; stray output inside the engine goes to stderr). UTF-8, at most x-max-line-bytes per line without the newline. Every message carries `v` (x-protocol-version), `id` and `op`; a reply adds `ok` and `result` or `error`, and may carry the engine's `decision`. `handshake` comes first. One request is answered before the next is read. Before its reply a request may send job messages with its `id` and `op`: progress (any number), `gate` (at most once; the engine then reads nothing but the sidecar's `proceed` for this request) and `committed` (only after `proceed`).

CommittedEvent.description: The save landed: its closed record is durable (engine-jobs §6.1 step 9).
CommittedEvent.title: CommittedEvent

Control.description: A line the sidecar sends that is not a request (it gets no reply).

CopyParams.description:
A confirmed copy (§8.2): the job's name (`.finzytrack.ft-<job>`), the target folder, the source ledger's root (as
the user named it), the files of `.finzytrack/` (the manifest, with the copy's new lineage id), the app's local data
folder (its `local/<key>/journal/` folders are read for `.open` journals) and the legacy write-lock files to try
(ADR-0062). Its answers are the create's (`CreateResult`, `CreateOutcomeResult`), with the copy's own reasons:
`legacy_saving`, `recovery_blocked`, `source_missing`, `source_unreadable`, `source_failed`, `number_failed` and
`beancount_failed` (Beancount's own load raised on the source: `path`, `detail` the line when known; S0098),
`encrypted`,
`source_changed`, `cannot_rewrite`, `cannot_place`, `load_differs`, `plugin_modules` (and `load_failed`,
`load_outside`). The same
params name the copy whose outcome `copy_outcome` reads.
CopyParams.title: CopyParams

CreateFile.description: One file of a new workspace: its path relative to the folder it is written in, and its text (UTF-8).
CreateFile.title: CreateFile

CreateOutcomeResult.description:
§1 "resolved from disk": `.finzytrack` after the target's sync holds the plan's bytes (`ours`), something else
(`foreign`), nothing (`absent`), or could not be read (`unknown`; `errno`); and `left`, the entries at the job's
names, whatever they hold (who made a name is not known after a death, so nothing is removed; null: not listed).
CreateOutcomeResult.title: CreateOutcomeResult

CreateParams.description:
A confirmed create (§8.2): the job's name (`.finzytrack.ft-<job>`), the target folder, the workspace's files,
which of them is the ledger's root, and the files of `.finzytrack/` (the manifest first among them). The same
params name the create whose outcome `create_outcome` reads.
CreateParams.title: CreateParams

CreateResult.description:
How the create ended (§8.2, §11). `created`: `.finzytrack/` holds the plan's bytes and is durable. `not_created`:
no `.finzytrack/` of ours stands there; `reason`: `not_empty`, `not_a_folder`, `no_parent`, `permission`, `taken`,
`read_back`, `load_failed`, `load_errors`, `load_outside`, `manifest_taken`, `path_moved`, `io_error`. `folder`:
the target as requested; `path`: the entry it is about; `detail`: the ACL entry, or how many load errors;
`errno`: the system's answer. `left`: what the job left in the folder after removing what it made, by path
relative to it, because it could not be sure each is only its own (empty: nothing of its own left; null: the
folder could not be cleaned up or listed, so the user is asked to check it).
CreateResult.title: CreateResult

Decision.description:
An engine decision, for the decision log (engine-jobs §12): the table and its version, its inputs and its
output. Content-free: the inputs are flat scalars (counts, which check failed, hash equalities), never a path, a
file name, an amount or a hash value; the engine is responsible for that, the shape keeps nesting out.
Decision.title: Decision

EntrySeen.description: An entry as it stands: its kind, and for a regular file its SHA-256 and size.
EntrySeen.title: EntrySeen

GateEvent.description: The job reached its commit point and waits for `proceed` (engine-jobs §4, §6.1 step 7).
GateEvent.title: GateEvent

HandshakeResult.description: What the engine is: the protocol it speaks and the versions that shape its answers.
HandshakeResult.title: HandshakeResult

InspectedFile.description:
What stands at one file of a stopped journal now, and its kept copies (§11: Show both, Show it).
`backup`: the path of a replaced file's backup when it is there and holds its old version, else null
(`recover_all.Inspected`; S0090).
InspectedFile.title: InspectedFile

JobEvent.description: A job message the engine sends before its reply.

JournalFile.description: One file a journal names: its canonical path, its `path_key`, and whether the save was creating it.
JournalFile.title: JournalFile

ListedJournal.description:
An `.open` record found by the listing. `readable` False: it names nothing it can be matched on (torn,
foreign, newer, of another name, or a read error: `errno`), so it blocks every open (ADR-0063).
ListedJournal.title: ListedJournal

NoParams.description: An op that takes no parameters.
NoParams.title: NoParams

OpenParams.description:
`open` (S0088; engine-jobs §2, §7; BL-0152): the overlay load of the ledger rooted at `root` and its publish
(`design/specs/mirror/publish.md` §4) into `<app cache>/workspaces/<workspace_key>/mirror/`, the app cache being
the folder the engine was started with (`--app-cache`; no request names it). No fingerprint: the load finds the
ledger set itself. `app_local_data` and `lineage` name the `.open` journals looked for; `floor`, `today` and
`built_at` as for `rebuild`.
OpenParams.title: OpenParams

OpenResult.description:
`open`'s answer: `loaded` (Beancount's result for the disk the load parsed; `entries` and `errors` its counts),
`moved` (the disk changed before the swap: nothing published; the sidecar runs the job again), `fresh` (the
published generation already describes the disk: nothing loaded), `paused` (an unfinished save's `.open` journal:
nothing published) or `refused` (nothing loaded: `refusal` says why, `refused` names the file and `line` the line
when known: `encrypted`, an encrypted file, ADR-0059; `number_failed` and `beancount_failed`, Beancount's own load
raised on the ledger, S0098; all three null otherwise). `publish`: what became of a
`loaded` result (`published`, or why not), `fresh` for `fresh`, null otherwise. `number` and `ledger_version`: the
current generation's when `publish` is `published` or `fresh`, else null. `removed`, `remove_failed`: the
cleanup's counts. It runs the ledger's plugins, so the engine is retired after it.
OpenResult.title: OpenResult

PingResult.description: The engine is up and reading requests.
PingResult.title: PingResult

PreviewError.description:
A new error the change brings (ADR-0067: listed, never a refusal): its key's SHA-256 (type, entry and message
without locations; `ledger.core.entry_keys`), Beancount's type name and message, and where Beancount puts it.
PreviewError.title: PreviewError

PreviewFile.description:
A file the plan writes: its path, the SHA-256 of its bytes now (`pre`) and of its new text (`post`), and the
new text (UTF-8, as `save`'s `post`).
PreviewFile.title: PreviewFile

PreviewParams.description:
`preview` (S0116): plan the change `request` asks of the mutator `mutator` on the published mirror generation
numbered `generation` (the one the plan was made on) of the ledger rooted at `root`, and check it with the
write-safety contract's steps before any write (`ledger.contract.prepare`). The mirror is read from the cache
folder the engine was started with (`--app-cache`; no request names it), under `workspace_key`; `app_local_data`
and `lineage` name the `.open` journals looked for. `request` is the mutator's own (its producer reads it); the
engine registers no producer yet, so every mutator is refused `unknown_mutator` until its slice adds one.
PreviewParams.title: PreviewParams

new_errors.message: Balance failed for 'Assets:Cash': expected 5 USD != accumulated 0 USD (5 too little)

PreviewResult.description:
`preview`'s answer. `prepared`: `files` (the write plan's texts and hashes), `fingerprint` (the plan's,
`ledger_set.encode`'s text, which the save's gate checks), `new_errors` (empty when the change brings none) and
`errors` (Beancount's errors in the candidate, as bean-check counts them). `refused`: `step` and `reason` say
where and why (`fault`: the step raised; `undecidable`: no result it could read), `path` the file when there is
one, `detail` more, without ledger content (led by what the load refused when it is no path: a plugin's name),
`line` the line when known (a load Beancount failed on). `moved`: the disk changed during the job (run it again
in a fresh engine). `paused`: an unfinished save's `.open` journal. `stale`: the published generation cannot be
the plan's baseline (`unpublished`: none, or not complete; `other_generation`: not the plan's; `not_fresh`: not
this ledger's, another engine build's, or the disk changed since it was built). It runs the ledger's plugins, so
the engine is retired after it; it writes nothing. A new error's `line` is null when Beancount gives none (it
puts some at line 0 or -1).
PreviewResult.title: PreviewResult

ProceedControl.description: The sidecar's answer to a gate: go past the commit point (engine-jobs §4).
ProceedControl.title: ProceedControl

ProgressEvent.description: The job's phase changed (engine-jobs §5.4: shown, never judged).
ProgressEvent.title: ProgressEvent

RebuildParams.description:
`rebuild` (S0070; engine-jobs §6.7, §7; ADR-0068 D1): Beancount's own load of the ledger rooted at `root`, the
ledger set named by `fingerprint` (`ledger_set.encode`'s text: the saved plan's, or the last try's answer)
observed before and after it, and its publish (S0087, BL-0113; `design/specs/mirror/publish.md` §4) into
`<app cache>/workspaces/<workspace_key>/mirror/`, the app cache being the folder the engine was started with
(`--app-cache`; no request names it): `app_local_data` and `lineage` name the `.open` journals looked
for at the re-check, `floor` is the highest generation number the sidecar saw this session (§3), `today` the
user's civil date (`meta.as_of`, INV-07) and `built_at` the instant.
RebuildParams.title: RebuildParams

RebuildResult.description:
`rebuild`'s answer: `loaded` (Beancount's result for the disk as observed; `entries` and `errors` its counts),
`moved` (the disk changed during the load or before the swap, or the load used files outside the set:
`fingerprint` is the set to try with next), `fresh` (the published generation already describes the disk: nothing
loaded or built) or `paused` (an unfinished save's `.open` journal at the re-check: not published). `publish`:
what became of a `loaded` result (`published`, or why not: `inexact`, `replaced`, `incomplete`), `fresh` for
`fresh`, null otherwise. `number` and `ledger_version`: the current generation's when `publish` is `published` or
`fresh`, else null. `removed`, `remove_failed`: the cleanup's counts. `refused` (S0098): Beancount's own load
raised on the ledger, nothing published: `refusal` says why (`number_failed`, its arithmetic failed on the
transaction `line` names; `beancount_failed`, any other failure), `refused` names the file and `line` the line
when known; all three are null otherwise. `errors` counts Beancount's errors, as bean-check does (the warnings on
numbers it rounded are rows of `ledger_errors`, not errors). It runs the ledger's plugins, so the engine is retired
after it.
RebuildResult.title: RebuildResult

RecoverActParams.description:
A blocked-screen action on one `.open` journal (§8.1 "Afterwards", §11): `keep`; `delete_kept` (`file`, the
kept copy's entry name `kept`, and the `sha256` the user was shown); `delete_created` (`file`, `sha256`).
RecoverActParams.title: RecoverActParams

RecoverListParams.description: `app_local_data`: the app's machine-local folder; the journals are in its `local/<key>/journal/`.
RecoverListParams.title: RecoverListParams

RecoverListResult.description: §8.1: every `.open` journal after a `durable_sync` of each journal folder; `.part` records removed.
RecoverListResult.title: RecoverListResult

RecoverTryResult.description:
One journal's try (§8.1 steps 2-4): `resolved`, `stopped` (blocking reason `stopped`) or `failed` (reason
`failed`), with the cause, the file (`path`), the entry that failed or blocked when it is not the file, the
blocking ACL entry (`detail`) and the error number; for `stopped`, what stands there now (`inspection`).
RecoverTryResult.title: RecoverTryResult

Refusal.description:
A refused request, or a line that was not a request. `id` and `op` are those of the request when it could
be read that far, else null; `op` is null too when it cannot be echoed exactly (not valid Unicode, or longer
than 128 characters).
Refusal.title: Refusal

SaveChange.description:
One file the save writes: its path as the ledger names it, the SHA-256 of its bytes in the plan (null: the save
creates it), and its new text (a ledger file is UTF-8 text; whole files until the contract's edits, BL-0106).
SaveChange.title: SaveChange

SaveConfine.description:
The test copy's folder as its mark recorded it when the copy was made (S0117 round 2; owner, 2026-11-14: "3"):
its real path, and its identity as the journal records a folder's (S0089): the drive's volume UUID, the file
system's type name and the folder's creation time in nanoseconds. The writer refuses unless the folder at that
path, with no link in it or above it, has that identity, and every file it writes lies inside it.
SaveConfine.title: SaveConfine

SaveOutcomeParams.description: §6.6: the save `session`-`job` of workspace `workspace_key`, whose engine ended without its final reply.
SaveOutcomeParams.title: SaveOutcomeParams

SaveOutcomeResult.description:
The record's state after its folder's sync (`unknown`: it could not be read; `errno`), and with no record, a
`.part` or `.resolved`, whether every target equals its pre bytes (`unchanged`; `path`: the first that does not).
SaveOutcomeResult.title: SaveOutcomeResult

SaveParams.description:
A confirmed plan (§2's `save`): who saves (`session`, `job`, the workspace's registry key and lineage id), the
ledger's root, the changes, the plan's fingerprint (`ledger_set.encode`'s text) and the app's machine-local folder.
The gate reads the published mirror in the app's cache folder the engine was started with (`--app-cache`;
`design/specs/mirror/publish.md` §7; S0087): no request names it. `confine` (S0117 rounds 1 and 2; owner,
2026-11-14: "Go with (2), fix it now", then "3"): the test copy's recorded folder (`SaveConfine`) that every file
the save writes must lie in, checked by the writer after the gate, else `not_saved {outside_folder}` with nothing
written; null for no confinement. Required, so a sender always says which.
SaveParams.title: SaveParams

SaveResult.description:
How the save ended (§6.1, §11). `saved`: the closed record is durable (`published`: the mirror was published,
never yet, BL-0113). `refused`: before the commit point, nothing written (`reason`: `unfinished_save`,
`ledger_changed`, `mirror_stale`, `encrypted_file`). `not_saved`: the writer's `NotSaved` (`reason` its own:
`hard_linked`, `locked`, `not_a_file`, `permission`, `changed`, `path_moved`, `read_back`, `io_error`,
`name_not_utf8`, `linked_folder`, `no_drive_id`, `no_folder_id`, `case_twins`, `folder_appeared`,
`app_folder_missing`, `outside_folder`, `link_in_copy`, `copy_folder_moved`, `copy_folder_missing`;
`open_journal`: writes are paused until
recovery). `unfinished`: a file may have been replaced and the rollback stopped (`cause`, and `cause_path` its
file: after `created_path_taken` the undo will ask about that file). `unchanged`: every file the save would write
was hashed again and equals its pre bytes; `changed`: the first file that re-hash found not at them (None also when
it could not read a file; S0100, BL-0163 (b)). `path`: the file it is about (the one an I/O error happened at);
`entry`: the folder a `permission` refusal is about, the link a `linked_folder` refusal names, the folder that
appeared (`folder_appeared`), the app's folder that is missing (`app_folder_missing`) or the folder the save is
confined to (`outside_folder`); `detail`: the ACL entry
that blocks it.
SaveResult.title: SaveResult

UnlistedFolder.description:
A journal folder that could not be synced, opened or listed: it blocks every open. `linked`: a link stands in
place of the key or journal folder (`folder` names the link) and it holds an `.open` record or could not be listed
through (S0077).
UnlistedFolder.title: UnlistedFolder
